evidence.quote: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (small)}} From {{inh|en|enm|minor}}, {{m|enm|menor}}, {{m|en|menour}}, etc., from {{der|en|la|minor||[[lesser]]; [[young]]; [[young]] [[person]]}} both directly and via {{der|en|nrf|-}} and {{der|en|frm|menor}}, {{m|frm|menour}}, etc. {{doublet|en|minus}} but not {{m|en|mini-}}. Cognate with {{m|en|minister}}, {{m|en|minify}}, {{m|en|Minorca}}, {{m|en|Menshevik}}{{,}} and possibly {{m|en|minnow}}. Compare {{cog|la|minimum}} and {{m|la|minuō}}, {{cog|goh|minniro}}, {{cog|kw|minow}}.

"Franciscan friar," literally "minor friar," from Latin minor "less, lesser, smaller,… See origin and meaning of minor. from Latin minor "less, lesser, smaller, junior," figuratively "inferior, less important," which was formed as a masculine/feminine form of minus on the mistaken assumption that minus was a neuter comparative, from PIE root *mei- (2) "small.
